newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off lows but still weak.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off lows but still weak.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures erased some of their early losses but ended well below the 20,000 mark on Thursday, suggesting scope for more moves to the downside.
The Nikkei 225 June contract shed 20 points to close at 19,810 after falling as low as 19,670 in early trade.
Dealers said the dollar's recovery against the yen had helped the market regain some ground but players were quick to sell into any strength.

"It looks like the daily trend has become more bearish on the technicals so the market came off even though the BOJ (Bank of Japan) keeps saying they're not going to hike rates now," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.

Japanese markets came under intense pressure on Wednesday after BOJ deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted as saying the central bank was mulling the right timing to raise the official discount rate, now at an all-time low of 0.50 percent.
A senior BOJ official later said Fukui had been misquoted and the central bank had no immediate plans for a rate rise.

News that the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd had incurred 10 billion yen in derivatives losses at its London branch had a limited impact as most players felt the bank was large enough to absorb this, dealers said.
"I think the Nikkei's going to stay below 20,000 for now. Any rebound above 19,900 will be a sell," the trader said.
The June Nikkei was likely to head lower on Friday, with support seen at 19,600 and then at 19,400, he added.
Taiwan stock index futures ended firmer in line with Taipei shares, which were boosted by strong buying in blue chip electronic counters.

The May MSCI contract ended at 351.6 against its opening 346.5 on volume of 1,511 lots. June ended up 5.4 points at 349.4 on 788 lots. Dealers said the May/June spread was actively traded ahead of May's expiry at the end of the month.
